stimulus.prompt: Which hazard do solder fumes mainly create?

page.learner_explanation: Naming the hazard is what makes the bench rules stick when you are concentrating on the joint.
page.learner_explanation_short: Naming the hazard is what makes the bench rules stick.
page.lesson_intent: Name the hazards before touching the iron.
page.section_title: Name the three burn and fume hazards at the bench

segments.body: Point at the iron, the fume path and your eyes, and name the hazard each one creates. Every rule on this bench exists to answer one of these three hazards, so you name them before you pick up the iron.
segments.heading: Point at each hazard
segments.short: Point at the iron, the fume path and your eyes.

segments.body: The three hazards are the hot iron, the solder fumes and flying clippings near the eyes. A hazard you cannot name is one you walk into while you are watching the joint, which is why the naming is its own habit.
segments.heading: Name the hazard before the iron
segments.short: The three hazards are the hot iron, the solder fumes and flying clippings.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. The three hazards are the hot iron, the solder fumes and flying clippings near the eyes.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: What temperature range suits leaded solder?

page.learner_explanation: Temperature is a time control: too cold means a longer touch and a colder joint.
page.lesson_intent: Teach the temperature setting for leaded solder.
page.section_title: Set an iron to the temperature a leaded joint needs

segments.body: Set the station, wait for the display to settle, and tin the tip before the first joint. The setting decides how long the iron sits on a joint, and a long touch is what damages pads and parts at the bench.
segments.heading: Set and tin before the first joint
segments.short: Set the station and wait for the display to settle.

segments.body: Leaded solder wants a moderate setting; hotter burns the flux before the joint forms. Turning the station hotter to work faster burns the flux first, and a joint with no flux goes cold even at temperature.
segments.heading: Hotter is not faster
segments.short: Leaded solder wants a moderate setting.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. Leaded solder wants a moderate setting; hotter burns the flux before the joint forms.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Set an iron to the temperature a leaded joint needs
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

page.learner_explanation: The code is positional, so reading order matters more than colour memory.
page.section_title: Read a resistor value from its colour bands

segments.body: Read the bands left to right, then multiply by the third band before you trust the value. Reading the code is how you know a part's value without trusting a label or a drawer.
segments.heading: Read the bands left to right
segments.short: Read the bands left to right.

segments.body: Brown, black, red, gold is ten times one hundred, so one thousand ohms at five percent. Read from the wrong end and the multiplier lands on the wrong band, so the reading always starts at the band nearest the end of the body.
segments.heading: Check the multiplier band
segments.short: Brown, black, red, gold is ten times one hundred.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. Brown, black, red, gold is ten times one hundred, so one thousand ohms at five percent.

worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: What does a lifted pad do under light pressure?

page.learner_explanation: A lifted pad turns a one-minute joint into a board repair, so it is checked before heat.
page.learner_explanation_short: A lifted pad turns a one-minute joint into a board repair.
page.section_title: Inspect a pad for lift before inserting a part

segments.body: Look at the pad edge against the board and press gently with a toothpick before you insert anything. A pad is the only thing holding the joint to the board, so its condition is checked before any heat goes near it.
segments.heading: Press the pad edge lightly
segments.short: Look at the pad edge against the board.

segments.body: A sound pad sits flat on the board; a lifted pad shows a shadow line and gives under light pressure. Pressing harder on a lifted pad tears it away completely, so the toothpick test is light and stops at the first give.
segments.heading: A lifted pad shows a shadow line
segments.short: A sound pad sits flat on the board.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. A sound pad sits flat on the board; a lifted pad shows a shadow line and gives under light pressure.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Inspect a pad for lift before inserting a part
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: Which side of the board should the bent lead sit on?

page.learner_explanation: A part that stands off the board strains its joints every time the board flexes.
page.learner_explanation_short: A part that stands off the board strains its joints.
page.section_title: Form a lead so the part seats flush

segments.body: Bend the lead with pliers at the board thickness and let the part drop flush without pushing it. The bend has to happen before soldering, because a lead bent while the joint is solid pulls on the pad.
segments.heading: Bend the lead at board thickness
segments.short: Bend the lead with pliers at the board thickness.

segments.body: The body sits flat with the lead bent between the body and the pad. Holding a part down with pliers while it cools still leaves it standing off the board later, so the lead carries the gap, not the tool.
segments.heading: The lead carries the gap
segments.short: The body sits flat with the lead bent.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. The body sits flat with the lead bent between the body and the pad.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Form a lead so the part seats flush
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: Which feature decides the part's orientation?

page.learner_explanation: Orientation errors survive soldering and only show up when the circuit does not work.
page.lesson_intent: Teach polarity against the board marking.
page.section_title: Insert a part in the right orientation

segments.body: Find the marking on the part and match it to the board's own marking before you bend anything. The marking is the only thing on the part that says which way the circuit expects it, and solder does not fix a reversed part.
segments.heading: Match the two markings
segments.short: Find the marking on the part and match it to the board's own marking.

segments.body: The part's marking and the board's marking face the same way. A reversed part can pass a visual check and still fail on power, which is why the markings are matched before anything is bent.
segments.heading: Solder does not fix a reversed part
segments.short: Both markings face the same way.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. The part's marking and the board's marking face the same way.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Insert a part in the right orientation
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

page.learner_explanation: Solder fed onto the tip makes a cold joint that looks finished and fails later.
page.learner_explanation_short: Solder fed onto the tip makes a cold joint.
page.section_title: Heat the pad and lead together before feeding solder

segments.body: Touch the tip to the pad and the lead at once, count two seconds, then feed solder into the joint, not the tip. The heat has to reach the joint before the solder is offered, or the solder sits on top of a cold surface.
segments.heading: Heat the joint, then feed solder
segments.short: Touch the tip to the pad and the lead at once.

segments.body: The joint reaches temperature first; solder follows the heat. Solder fed onto the tip runs down hot and looks joined, and the same joint fails a continuity check once it has cooled to room temperature.
segments.heading: Solder on the tip looks joined
segments.short: The joint reaches temperature first.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. The joint reaches temperature first; solder follows the heat.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Heat the pad and lead together before feeding solder
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: What does a cold joint look like?

page.learner_explanation: Surface is the cheapest inspection you have, and it is read before power is applied.
page.learner_explanation_short: Surface is the cheapest inspection you have.
page.section_title: Recognise a cold joint from its surface

segments.body: Compare a grainy joint with a bright fillet and say which one moved while it cooled. Most cold joints are readable without a meter, and the surface is the first inspection you can do at your own bench.
segments.heading: Compare grainy with bright
segments.short: Compare a grainy joint with a bright fillet.

segments.body: A cold joint has a grainy, matte surface; a sound fillet is bright and concave. A bright joint can still be cold under the surface, so the grainy ones are the ones you rework before testing the rest.
segments.heading: Rework the grainy ones first
segments.short: A cold joint has a grainy, matte surface.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. A cold joint has a grainy, matte surface; a sound fillet is bright and concave.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Recognise a cold joint from its surface
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

page.learner_explanation: Applying one criterion to many joints is the skill; the criterion itself does not change.
page.learner_explanation_short: Applying one criterion to many joints is the skill.
page.lesson_intent: Apply the criterion to a real joint.
page.section_title: Inspect a finished joint against the fillet criterion

segments.body: Judge each joint on the board against the fillet criterion and mark the ones that need rework. One criterion applied to every joint is what keeps the inspection consistent, instead of judging each joint on how it feels.
segments.heading: Judge every joint by one criterion
segments.short: Judge each joint on the board against the fillet criterion.

segments.body: A sound joint is shiny, concave and covers the pad without a ball. A balled joint is the clearest fail and the easiest to under-call, because it looks like extra solder rather than a bad joint.
segments.heading: A balled joint is a fail
segments.short: A sound joint is shiny, concave and covers the pad.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. A sound joint is shiny, concave and covers the pad without a ball.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Inspect a finished joint against the fillet criterion
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: When do you lift the wick?

page.learner_explanation: Pulling the wick while the solder is solid is how pads lift.
page.learner_explanation_short: Pulling the wick while the solder is solid lifts pads.
page.section_title: Wick a solder bridge without lifting the pad

segments.body: Add flux, lay the wick over the bridge, and heat the wick until the solder flows into it before lifting. A bridge connects two points the circuit keeps apart, so it is removed before power is ever applied.
segments.heading: Lay the wick over the bridge
segments.short: Add flux and lay the wick over the bridge.

segments.body: Heat through the wick and stop as soon as the bridge disappears. Lifting the wick early leaves solder behind and pulls on a solid joint, so the wick comes up only after the solder has flowed into it.
segments.heading: Lift only after the solder flows
segments.short: Heat through the wick and stop.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. Heat through the wick and stop as soon as the bridge disappears.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Wick a solder bridge without lifting the pad
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: Why add fresh solder before desoldering?

page.learner_explanation: Old solder has lost its flux, so adding fresh solder is what makes removal quick.
page.learner_explanation_short: Old solder has lost its flux.
page.section_title: Desolder a two-lead part without overheating it

segments.body: Add fresh solder to each joint, alternate heat between the leads, and pull gently once both are molten. Fresh solder restores the flux that makes the old joint flow, so removal stays quick instead of holding heat on the pads.
segments.heading: Add fresh solder to each joint
segments.short: Add fresh solder to each joint and alternate heat between the leads.

segments.body: Fresh solder and alternating heat keep the part and the pads alive. Holding heat on one lead while the other is still solid lifts pads and cooks the part, so the heat alternates.
segments.heading: Alternate the heat
segments.short: Fresh solder and alternating heat keep the pads alive.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. Fresh solder and alternating heat keep the part and the pads alive.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Desolder a two-lead part without overheating it
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.

check.learner_instructions: Answer in one short phrase, without notes.

stimulus.prompt: Which meter setting proves the repair conducts?

page.learner_explanation: A joint can look right and still be open; the meter is the check the eye cannot make.
page.learner_explanation_short: A joint can look right and still be open.
page.section_title: Prove continuity with a meter after rework

segments.body: Set the meter to continuity, probe the two ends of the repaired path, and confirm the beep before power. The meter answers the one question the eye cannot: does the repair conduct from one intended point to the other.
segments.heading: Probe the ends of the repaired path
segments.short: Set the meter to continuity and probe the two ends.

segments.body: Continuity between the intended points proves the repair conducts. Continuity across the wrong two points proves nothing, so the probes go on the ends of the repaired path, not on the nearest metal.
segments.heading: Continuity across the wrong points
segments.short: Continuity proves the repair conducts.

worked_example.answer: The step is done and checked. Continuity between the intended points proves the repair conducts.
worked_example.prompt: A worked example of Prove continuity with a meter after rework
worked_example.short: The step is done and checked.
